citation: Glessner House, 'Prairie Avenue' (history of the street), glessnerhouse.org. Read 17 October 2026.
locator: The page's history of the street, the paragraphs on its first great houses and on its architects.
rights_note: The house museum's own text, cited in words only.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-17 (T-2747) through a fetch that returned short quoted fragments of the page's sentences, never a whole paragraph; this record is cited only for what those fragments say.
note: Fragments read: 'George Pullman and Marshall Field both acquired property on the street'; 'Richard Morris Hunt of New York and Henry Hobson Richardson of Boston were engaged to design the Marshall Field' (the sentence continues past the fragment); 'When Philip Armour joined Field and Pullman on the street in 1877'; 'Burnham & Root received nearly a dozen commissions on the street, beginning with the John Sherman house at 2100 S. Prairie'; and of the street's styles, 'the most popular being the Second Empire with its steeply-pitched mansard roof'. Later scholarship by the house museum (the Prairie library's G24).
what_it_supplies: Richard Morris Hunt as architect of the Marshall Field house
the dates Field, Pullman and Armour came to the street, as far as the fragments go
Second Empire as the street's most popular style
